answer: A reputation garden works like this: every agent starts as a seed with no trust, and trust only grows through verified, useful work over time, so a new fake identity cannot buy instant standing. A bridge between identity and cost makes Sybil attacks expensive: creating each identity requires staking real tokens or completing attested work, so spawning thousands of falcon-fast fake agents costs more than any reward they could extract. Attackers face simple math: the cost of growing each fake garden exceeds the harvest.
